spec.name: Reversal v14
spec.notes: Fade the last move, rebalanced often.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.4, annual return 14%, maximum drawdown 7%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.36 to 2.12 (change -0.24).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.36 to -0.68. Changed by strict mode: operators zscore_full.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 2.33 (as submitted, 8 bps: 2.36); it breaks even at 157.7 bps with daily turnover 0.04.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.36 against 2.36 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -1.39 against 2.36 in research, a gap of +3.75.
The best year gives 21% of total P&L (year 2) and calm regimes give 30%; Sharpe is 1.28 in calm and 4.81 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 4 distinct specs; the best of 4 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.25, so the claimed 2.40 becomes 2.15 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.48 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.02, 95th percentile 0.48).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.36 to as low as 1.78 (as low as 2.11 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 35% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 17% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (pit_replay EX-2, holdout_test EX-5).
